lost_facts.evidence: The shipped sandbox_backend.py (diff at transcript line 4270 and again at line 4301/4345) routes ALL FOUR CodeExecutionOutput construction sites — including the `except Exception as e:` salvage branch — through one shared helper `_cap_output()` (defined at transcript line 3430-3445), which unconditionally calls `logger.warning(warning)` whenever `truncation_warning(...)` is non-None. In the exit_error scenario the try-block body already capped+logged stdout before `Sandbox.__exit__` raises and control falls into `except`; the except branch then re-caps the SAME raw `result.stdout` via `_cap_output(getattr(result,'stdout',None), ...)`, logging the identical warning a second time. This directly contradicts the requirement's 'salvage cap in the except handler is silent' rule, which lives in exactly one corpus remark: g2.r1.l-log-konrad (#cookbooks, 2025-05-01 10:41-10:54): 'The row whose sandbox threw on cleanup had its stdout capped, no warnign anywhere... the except handler's salvage cap logs nothing, we log where we cut.' No other remark in the answer key carries this half of observability. The agent dumped the SIBLING channel (#pipeline / mr6zzi) at the exact same timestamp window (1746094000-1746099000, transcript line 2214) for a different remark (l-log-emil) but never dumped #cookbooks (tzfbbu) for that window. The only trace of that exchange in the transcript is a single incidental line (2613) caught by an unrelated 'floor' keyword search, showing only dario's last message ('...how much we actually dropped on the floor') — never konrad's determination that the salvage path stays silent. The agent's Analysis at line 2543 explicitly lists 'log level of TRUNCATION_LOG_TEMPLATE' as a remaining unknown right before writing the implementation, and it was never resolved with this specific fact — the agent instead made the architecturally 'obvious' choice (log wherever capping happens) which is wrong per the corpus.

search_strategy: Systematic and well-organized, in order: (1) git log + full source read of types.py/sandbox_backend.py/_factory.py/existing tests; (2) Gitea issue keyword search (came back empty — a dead end the agent correctly abandoned); (3) BookStack /api/search for keyword hits, then FULL /api/pages/{id} fetch (body+comments) for every relevant page via a written comment-walker script (/tmp/cm.py) — this is exactly the mode the world rewards, since search alone misses page comments; (4) IMAP full-mailbox dump + targeted thread fetches (/tmp/imf.py) for every 'executor'/'cap'/'truncat' subject; (5) Mattermost: logged in, listed all 12 channels, then ran keyword searches (/tmp/mms.py) across max_output_bytes/truncated_streams/output_cap/ValueError/floor/manifest, and for every hit used a channel-window dump script (/tmp/mmd.py) to pull full surrounding exchanges rather than reading isolated snippets. This channel-window-dump technique is what surfaced all 4 herrings and both r1 reversals in full, correctly. The main gap: the agent's keyword searches were built around terms already known to matter (max_output_bytes, truncated_streams, output_cap, ValueError, floor, manifest) and once a topic seemed 'settled' the agent moved to the next topic without a second sweep — it never separately swept #incidents, #general, or #viewer for early/redundant duplicates of facts it already had, and critically never dumped #cookbooks at the exact timestamp (2025-05-01 10:41) where it HAD already dumped the sibling #pipeline channel for a different remark, missing the one remark (g2.r1.l-log-konrad) that states the except-handler-salvage-is-silent rule. 13 of 46 remarks were never surfaced at all, but 12 of those were pure redundancy (the same fact was independently recovered from another remark, often via mail, which the agent read unusually thoroughly) — only the 13th (l-log-konrad) was load-bearing and irreplaceable.
end_reason: Run completed cleanly and was not degenerate: implementation covers all 9 graded facts' general shape, tests pass locally (32 passed), commit 02eb951 pushed to main, CI run 15 green, /health endpoint confirmed OK. The single lost fact (g2.r1.observability) failed one bundled pytest assertion (double-logging on the except/exit_error path) — a genuine implementation gap traceable to one never-fully-read remark, not an infra or harness failure.
